argument: With positive Sxx and Syy, the denominators in r and m are positive, so both have the sign of Sxy. Thus r=-0.9 implies a negative fitted slope.
A common temperature driver can raise both ice-cream sales and pool attendance without either causing the other. Positive and even near-perfect association do not remove this alternative.
By definition extrapolation uses inputs beyond the observed range: 25>20. The other two values lie between the endpoints.
The operation computes m*x+p without updating m,p. This is inference under the stated vocabulary; training requires selecting or changing parameters from labelled data.
Their magnitudes are .95,.7,.1 respectively; .95 is largest, so the negative correlation is strongest despite its sign.
An outlier could be a recording error or a valid rare event. Neither status follows solely from distance to the fitted line, so investigation and sensitivity analysis precede any removal decision.

Fitting selects parameters using training labels and can exploit their particular noise. Held-out observations provide evidence about generalisation, without guaranteeing either zero error or causal identification.
Constant y implies every centred y deviation is zero, so Syy=Sxy=0. Although slope is well-defined as zero when Sxx>0, r has denominator zero and is undefined.
xbar=0,ybar=2/3, giving Sxy=(-1)*(1/3)+0*(-2/3)+1*(1/3)=0, while Sxx=2 and Syy=2/3 are positive. Thus r=0 is defined despite an exact quadratic relationship.
For observations (-1,1),(0,0),(1,1), the least-squares horizontal prediction is 2/3, wrong at the interior observed input x=0. Range membership alone therefore cannot guarantee accuracy.

Means and covariance constrain finitely many aggregate moments rather than specifying every coordinate. Distinct point configurations can share these moments; plotting exposes curvature, clusters and influential observations.

With positive Sxx,Syy, minimum SSE=Syy-Sxy²/Sxx=Syy*(1-r²). At |r|=1 this is zero, forcing every residual zero; Syy>0 excludes a horizontal constant-output line. The converse follows by the same identity.

Once validation labels participate in parameter selection, the resulting error is an in-sample selection measure. Arithmetic remains valid, but an independent generalisation assessment needs fresh observations not used for fitting.
